per_window.ps-ns: no_evidence_in_window for large fast motion in SH3-3. The BMRB 7036 source paper, now read in full (free SH3-3, 20 °C, pH 6.8, 50 mM phosphate with DTT, 800 MHz), reports heteronuclear NOE above 0.7 at most residues despite a far-UV CD spectrum typical of an unstructured protein, and its model-free analysis failed, returning order parameters no higher than about 0.3 with large exchange terms under every diffusion model (R7036-J1). The SH3-2 domain measured alongside fits cleanly with S2 above 0.8 (J13). Other-domain context: native SH3-1 is ordered apart from its termini, T33 and loop tips (J5), and acidified or 4AlaMut SH3-1 has more fast motion (J6, J7; 278 K, 800 MHz).
per_window.us-ms: unresolved and contested. In the reference state the average T2 is about 80 ms against about 100 ms for SH3-2 under identical conditions and the HSQC lines are visibly broader, which the authors read as us-ms conformational exchange; only one set of peaks is present, so they place the exchange faster than the chemical-shift timescale (J2). The same authors keep dynamic aggregation as an alternative, undetected by CD and by the protein and DTT concentration checks, and the T1 values exclude a stable dimer but not every oligomer (J12, artefact_suspected, conflicting with J2). In the linked SH3-2-SH3-3 construct resonance loss blocked the assignment and was also ascribed to exchange (J14). The remaining us-ms statements concern the SH2 domain with phosphoephrinB2 peptides bound, abstract only (J10, J11).
per_window.slower_than_ms: search_insufficient (J3): neither the full text nor any other row gives hydrogen exchange, folding or another slower-than-millisecond rate for SH3-3.
per_window.undetermined: Peptide titrations lose some peaks and give trajectories a two-site model cannot fit, pooled over domains and peptides (J15). The three SH3-3 structures 2FRY, 1WX6 and 1U5S share a core and differ at the termini of the LIM4 complex (J16). The ultraweak SH3-3/PINCH-1 LIM4 complex (KD about 3 mM, abstract; J4) is binding, not conformational exchange. Acidified and 4AlaMut SH3-1 populate non-native two-helix states (J8, J9). Not judged: the static SH3-1 versus Src SH3 packing comparison (r10), which proposes a folding requirement without kinetics.

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Unknown, with a lead: free Nck2 SH3-3 at 20 °C, pH 6.8 in 50 mM phosphate with 5 mM DTT (800 MHz) has an average T2 of about 80 ms against about 100 ms for the neighbouring SH3-2 domain measured the same way, with visibly broader HSQC lines, which the authors attribute to microsecond-to-millisecond conformational exchange and/or dynamic aggregation; no residue, rate, population or chemical-shift difference is given, the model-free fit failed, and no Rex is reported, and the single set of peaks places any exchange faster than the chemical-shift timescale.
open_conflicts: Free SH3-3, us-ms: conformational exchange (R7036-J2) versus dynamic aggregation (R7036-J12) as the source of the short T2 and the broad lines; the authors raise both and exclude neither, and no concentration-resolved relaxation measurement exists.
questions_for_gina: The source paper's model-free fit of SH3-3 failed (order parameters of about 0.3 with large exchange terms) and the authors could not separate conformational exchange from dynamic aggregation: should the atlas record this entry as exchange detected, or hold it until a concentration series or a dispersion experiment exists?
Should SH3-1 and SH2 rows from other Nck2 domains be kept as inference_from_homolog context, or excluded from this entry altogether?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The BMRB 7036 source paper (doi:10.1021/bi060091y, Liu et al. 2006) was read in full on 2026-10-20 (case S6_r6_7036_20261020223524), superseding the abstract-only row R7036-r1, which is no longer cited. Its SH3-3 samples are in 50 mM sodium phosphate at pH 6.8 and 20 °C with 0.01% azide and 5 mM DTT; the relaxation sample concentration is not stated and the per-residue T1, T2 and NOE profiles exist only in Figures 9 and 10, so no residue list or numerical value can be assigned. The same paper's SH3-2 and the linked SH3-2-SH3-3 construct are different samples, and the SH3-1 rows (5 mM phosphate, 278 K, 800 MHz, deliberate acid or four-alanine mutation) and the SH2 peptide rows are other domains; none sets an SH3-3 verdict. NMR and ITC affinities in that paper disagree and the buffers differ, which is unresolved. No deposition readback file exists for this entry.

detection.method: 15N T1, T2 and {1H}-15N steady-state NOE at 800 MHz; model-free analysis attempted with Modelfree 4.15 and Tensor
detection.observable: heteronuclear NOE above 0.7 at most residues; the model-free fits with isotropic, axially symmetric and fully asymmetric diffusion all returned order parameters no higher than about 0.3 together with large exchange terms, which the authors call strange and unsatisfactory
detection.detection_window: 15N T1, T2 and NOE at one field, 800 MHz, 20 °C, pH 6.8; the heteronuclear NOE reports motion faster than the tumbling time, so hNOE above 0.7 excludes large-amplitude sub-nanosecond motion at those sites but says nothing about us-ms exchange or about residues whose peaks are too broad or overlapped to measure. No order parameter can be quoted, because the model-free fit did not converge to a physically sensible solution, and the per-residue values exist only as a figure.

judgments.reason: Full text of the BMRB 7036 source paper (Liu et al. 2006): the isolated SH3-3 domain has heteronuclear NOE above 0.7 at most residues despite a far-UV CD spectrum typical of an unstructured protein, so large fast backbone motion is not detected; the model-free analysis that would give order parameters failed, returning S2 no higher than about 0.3 with large exchange terms under every diffusion model (sources_cache/10.1021_bi060091y.pdf, pp. 7178-7180, 7182, Figure 10).

detection.method: 15N T2 and HSQC line widths at one field, compared with the SH3-2 domain under the same conditions; model-free fitting attempted but rejected by the authors; no dispersion, R1rho or CEST experiment
detection.observable: shortened average T2 (about 80 ms) and broad HSQC lines; large but unreliable exchange terms in the failed model-free fit

judgments.reason: Full text: the authors read the short average T2 and the broad lines of free SH3-3 as conformational exchange on the microsecond-to-millisecond timescale, and note that only one set of HSQC peaks is present, which they take to mean the exchange is faster than the chemical-shift timescale; exchange is detected in the reference state, but no rate, population or chemical-shift difference exists, the model-free exchange terms come with unphysical order parameters, and the authors keep dynamic aggregation as an alternative explanation (R7036-J12). Single-field exchange broadening can also come from anisotropic tumbling; a dispersion experiment would confirm (sources_cache/10.1021_bi060091y.pdf, pp. 7178-7180).
